# Your List of Saves

#### Course: Practical Git and GitHub

## Your List of Saves

To see your history, run:

```python
$ git log
```

Output

```text
commit 9c2f4a1b3e8d7f6c5a0b2e4d1f3a7c9b5e2d4f6a Author: Abidit Shrestha abidit@example.com Date:   Thu Oct 12 23:47:02 2023 +0545

    Rework homepage layout

commit 4f3a1b2c5e7d9f1a3b5c7d9e1f3a5b7c9d1e3f5

Author: Abidit Shrestha <abidit@example.com>

Date:   Mon Oct 9 10:05:44 2023 +0545
    Add homepage and stylesheet
```

You will see a list of all your commits, most recent first.

Each entry shows:

- a unique ID
- the message you wrote
- the date it was created

That long string of letters and numbers is the commit ID. It uniquely identifies that version.

For daily use, this view is too detailed. Use:

```python
$ git log --oneline
```

Output

```text
9c2f4a1 Rework homepage layout 4f3a1b2 Add homepage and stylesheet
```

Now you see a short ID and the message. That's usually enough.
